title: Th’ Atoning Work Is Done
description: Th’ Atoning Work Is Done in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Kelly wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 241.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Th’a-ton-ing work is done, The Vic-tim’s blood is shed, And Je-sus now is gone His peo-ple’s cause to plead: He stands in heaven their great High Priest And bears their names up-on His breast.

lines: He stands in heaven their great High Priest
And bears their names upon His breast.
But justice now withstands no more,
And mercy yields her boundless store.
In Him the shadows of the Law
Are all fulfilled and now withdraw.
Hid from the eyes of men,
In brightest glory He will come
And take His waiting people home.

licence: Public domain: Thomas Kelly died in 1855.
credits: Words by Thomas Kelly (1769–1855), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
